findings.issue_text: English file path derivation regex `replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")` doesn't match unsuffixed default bundles like `messages.properties`, so the file is treated as its own English source and any HTML in it is self-permitted
Unconditional RuntimeException on missing English file crashes the Maven build for bundles whose `_en` variant doesn't exist in `resources` (e.g. custom theme directories) instead of reporting

`containsHtml(englishValue)` gates POLICY_SOME_HTML which only whitelists element names, so the check verifies 'some allowed HTML' rather than 'same HTML as English' (e.g. `

` in translation where English has `
` passes)

ANCHOR_PATTERN `</?a[^>]*>` also matches `<abbr>`, `<address>`, `<area>`, `<audio>`, `<applet>`, so an English `<audio>` tag legitimizes a translated `<audio src=... onerror=...>`; should be tightened to `</?a(\s[^>]*)?>`

`santizeAnchors` iterates the matcher over the original `value` while `value` is reassigned via replaceFirst, so matching continues on a stale string and reordered identical anchors with different hrefs are not distinguishable; should collect anchors into lists and compare
`sanitized.replace("<!-- -->", "")` and `unescapeHtml4` post-processing let a translation literally containing `<!-- -->` or entities like `<script>` compare equal to its sanitized form and pass
`normalizeValue` unescapes the raw value so `<b>` in a translation becomes `<b>` and is flagged as illegal HTML even though it renders as text (false positive)

PropertyResourceBundle loaded from a FileInputStream uses JDK-dependent encoding (ISO-8859-1 or UTF-8 fallback), so multi-byte characters may be mangled and reported as illegal HTML; should use InputStreamReader with UTF-8
Lithuanian `totpStep1` in messages_lt.properties was replaced with an Italian sentence (wrong language shipped to users)
Simplified Chinese `totpStep1` in messages_zh_CN.properties uses Traditional Chinese characters, inconsistent with the rest of the file

`commons-text` 1.13.0 hard-coded in theme-verifier pom.xml transitively pulls `commons-lang3` which may conflict with the Keycloak parent's managed version; should be managed via root dependencyManagement

No test covers the positive path where a translation with allowed HTML matching English (``, `
`, identical ``) produces no messages
No test for the `resources-community` to `resources` path rewrite or the missing-English-file crash
No test for the `choice` normalization that the PR relied on for `error-invalid-multivalued-size`

Diff-trimming loop (lines 100-108) can make `start > value.length() - end` when one string is a prefix/suffix of the other, causing `substring` to throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException and abort verification; clamp `end` to `min(value.length(), sanitized.length()) - start`

`file.getAbsolutePath().contains("email")` heuristic matches any parent directory containing 'email' (e.g. a developer's checkout path), changing verification behavior; should match on the theme sub-path `/email/messages/`

adjudication_records.issue_text: English file path derivation regex `replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")` doesn't match unsuffixed default bundles like `messages.properties`, so the file is treated as its own English source and any HTML in it is self-permitted
Unconditional RuntimeException on missing English file crashes the Maven build for bundles whose `_en` variant doesn't exist in `resources` (e.g. custom theme directories) instead of reporting

adjudication.rationale: In verifySafeHtml(), the code always derives an "englishFile" path and then unconditionally tries to open it with `new FileInputStream(englishFile)`. If that file does not exist or is unreadable, the `IOException` is caught and rethrown as a `RuntimeException` (`throw new RuntimeException("unable to read file " + englishFile, e);`). This exception is not caught by `verify()` (which only catches `IOException` around `Files.readString`), so it will abort the verifier run/build instead of adding a message to `messages`. Therefore, missing corresponding `_en.properties` files will crash the Maven build as described.

adjudication.rationale:
The diff shows `containsHtml(englishValue)` is used only to decide between `POLICY_SOME_HTML` (allows `br,p,strong,b`) and `POLICY_NO_HTML`. It does not attempt to enforce that the translation uses the *same* tags as English, only that HTML is permitted at all when English contains any HTML (per the in-code comment: “Only if the English source string contains HTML we also allow HTML in the translation”). Therefore the observation that `

` could be used when English had `
` is true, but calling it a “problem” assumes an unstated requirement (tag-for-tag equivalence) that is not evidenced in the diff.

PropertyResourceBundle loaded from a FileInputStream uses JDK-dependent encoding (ISO-8859-1 or UTF-8 fallback), so multi-byte characters may be mangled and reported as illegal HTML; should use InputStreamReader with UTF-8

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds verifySafeHtml(), which loads both the target and English .properties files via `new PropertyResourceBundle(new FileInputStream(...))`. The `PropertyResourceBundle(InputStream)` constructor expects ISO-8859-1 encoded properties (per JDK spec), not UTF-8. The repository’s message files clearly contain non-ASCII characters (e.g., Chinese, Persian, etc. in the diff), which would be mis-decoded/mangled when read this way, potentially causing incorrect comparisons/sanitization results and false “Illegal HTML” reports. Using `PropertyResourceBundle(Reader)` with an explicit UTF-8 `InputStreamReader` would avoid this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `commons-text` 1.13.0 hard-coded in theme-verifier pom.xml transitively pulls `commons-lang3` which may conflict with the Keycloak parent's managed version; should be managed via root dependencyManagement

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add an explicit `org.apache.commons:commons-text` dependency with a hard-coded version (1.13.0) in `misc/theme-verifier/pom.xml`, but the proposed finding hinges on two unverified assumptions not shown in the diff: (1) that Keycloak’s parent/root POM manages a different `commons-lang3` (or `commons-text`) version via dependencyManagement, and (2) that the transitive `commons-lang3` version brought by `commons-text` would actually cause a conflict or incorrect build/runtime behavior. From the diff alone, we cannot confirm any version mismatch, conflict, or resulting defect—only that a version is specified locally.

adjudication.rationale:
The added tests in VerifyMessagePropertiesTest only assert failure cases: illegalHtmlTag_en.properties (illegal HTML), noHtml_de.properties (HTML in translation when English has none), and changedAnchor_de.properties (anchor mismatch). There is no test fixture where the English value contains allowed HTML (e.g., /
/

or an tag) and the translation contains the same allowed HTML so that verifySafeHtml() produces an empty/clean result. This positive-path behavior (POLICY_SOME_HTML and matching anchors) is therefore untested in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test for the `resources-community` to `resources` path rewrite or the missing-English-file crash

adjudication.rationale: In `VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml()`, the code unconditionally derives an `englishFile` path via `file.getAbsolutePath().replaceAll("resources-community", "resources").replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")` and then tries to load it with `new FileInputStream(englishFile)`. Any `IOException` (including file-not-found) is rethrown as a `RuntimeException`, so a missing English file will crash verification. The newly added tests only cover cases where an `_en.properties` fixture exists alongside the locale file (`noHtml_de` with `noHtml_en`, `changedAnchor_de` with `changedAnchor_en`) and don’t exercise the `resources-community`→`resources` rewrite path or the missing-English-file behavior. So the finding is verifiably true from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test for the `choice` normalization that the PR relied on for `error-invalid-multivalued-size`

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new normalization logic in `normalizeValue()` specifically to handle ICU `choice` patterns for keys including `error-invalid-multivalued-size` (`key.equals("error-invalid-multivalued-size")`) by replacing `\{[0-9]+,choice,[^}]*}` with `...`. This normalization is relied upon because the PR also changes `error-invalid-multivalued-size` messages to include a `{2,choice,...|1<values}` fragment. However, the added tests cover duplicate keys, illegal HTML tags, disallowing HTML when English has none, and changed anchors; none exercise the `choice` normalization path (no fixture/message includes a `{n,choice,...}` pattern or the `error-invalid-multivalued-size` key). So the finding that there is no test for this relied-on normalization is verifiably true from the diff.

`file.getAbsolutePath().contains("email")` heuristic matches any parent directory containing 'email' (e.g. a developer's checkout path), changing verification behavior; should match on the theme sub-path `/email/messages/`

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `normalizeValue()`, the behavior is gated by `if (file.getAbsolutePath().contains("email"))`, which uses an absolute path substring match. This can unintentionally trigger for non-email message bundles if any parent directory in the checkout/build path happens to contain the string "email" (e.g., `/home/user/email/...`). When triggered, it strips ` style="direction: rtl;"` from values, altering verification results (potential false negatives) for files that are not actually under the theme email messages path. A path-specific check (e.g., matching `.../email/messages/...` in the project-relative path) would avoid this environment-dependent behavior.
